subject: Cache rewrite Oct 29 — request to exclude maintenance from SLA calculation
messages:
From: Claire Thomas <claire@edgewave.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Cache rewrite Oct 29 — request to exclude maintenance from SLA calculation

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this — we just finished a post-mortem on Oct 29 when we pushed a cache rewrite and saw a ~30-40 minute window of elevated errors and latency that impacted our users. Our infra team believes the disruption was caused by an in-place cache rewrite we triggered to change TTLs, and we didn’t receive a Redwood maintenance notification. Per the contract we expect customer-driven maintenance to be excluded from SLA calculations if we notify in advance; we didn’t in this case because of the rush rollout.

Can you confirm how Redwood is attributing that window? The attached edgewave-outage-log.csv contains our timing and sample traces from our side. We are requesting the degradation period be excluded from uptime for the purpose of credit calculation, or for Redwood to apply the standard customer-maintenance exclusion.

If you need additional traces, we can include request IDs and the exact API keys. We’d like to resolve credit calculation and avoid escalations — happy to join a quick call.

Best,
Claire Thomas
Head of Infrastructure — EdgeWave Ltd.
claire@edgewave.com

Attachment: edgewave-outage-log.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Claire Thomas <claire@edgewave.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Cache rewrite Oct 29 — request to exclude maintenance from SLA calculation

Claire — thanks for the quick context and the log. We’ll investigate immediately. A couple of quick notes while we look:

- Per Section 3.2 of the SLA, planned maintenance windows initiated by the customer can be excluded from uptime only when a prior notice is sent to Redwood support and the maintenance is tagged against the affected API keys.
- Unplanned or customer-side actions that produce backend errors without advance notice are usually treated as incidents for credit calculation unless telemetry shows clear origin outside Redwood’s serving path.

I’ve asked our infra team to pull edge traces, router metrics, and per-node 5xx rates for the window you flagged. Can you do two quick things for us:
1) Send a few example request IDs (x-request-id) from the CSV that saw 5xx responses, and
2) Confirm which API key(s) correspond to the production rollout you mentioned.

We’ll aim to come back with an attribution recommendation within 48 hours. If we find the root cause is fully customer-initiated and external to our edge runtime, we will exclude it from SLA uptime calculation. If not, we’ll propose an apportionment.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 14:45:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Cache rewrite Oct 29 — internal: attribution recommendation

Laura / Sean — pulling together the telemetry from Oct 29. Summary of our findings:

- Customer CSV shows a cluster of failed requests between 07:14 and 07:46 UTC.
- Redwood edge metrics show a spike in 5xx rate across three edge POPs that route that customer’s traffic (5xx peaked at ~8% for the hour).
- Traces show error origins in our HTTP proxy layer (503s from our cache eviction path) for ~28 minutes; however, request flow also indicates a burst of concurrent cache writes initiated by a non-standard client signature that matches the customer’s rollout.

Given mixed signals (part customer-initiated writes + proxy-level 503s), my recommended approach is:
1) Treat the incident as a partial degradation rather than full outage.
2) Apply apportionment: calculate the customer-initiated fraction by sampling request volume tagged with their roll-out signature and exclude that fraction from the downtime window. For the remainder (proxy-derived errors) Redwood counts as downtime.

Preliminary apportionment: total affected minute-weighted requests = 12,300; estimated customer-side writes = 3,690 -> customer fraction = 30%; Redwood fraction = 70%. Using our standard SLA credit formula (downtime minutes × Redwood fraction) -> recommend 30 minutes × 0.70 = 21 minutes of chargeable downtime. Under the SLA credit table that maps minutes to credit % we’d land at a 40% service credit for the month.

I propose we offer 40% credit and a one-time exception to waive the advance-notice requirement this time — rationale: customer rollout triggered by an urgent business need, and telemetry shows blended causality. We should also offer an Ops review to walk through mitigations for next rollouts.

Questions: Do we want to make the waiver conditional on the customer signing a short rollback/ops-playbook addendum (attached signed-bridge-agreement.pdf draft)? If yes, I’ll pass to legal and CS to prepare.

-Markus

Attachment: edgewave-credit-calculation.csv (CSV, 3KB)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Cache rewrite Oct 29 — internal: approval

Thanks Markus — I agree with your recommendation and the customer-facing framing. Offering 40% credit and an Ops review is reasonable. A couple of operational asks before we commit:
- Please confirm the precise minutes we will report in the credit calculation and the associated HubSpot deal (EDGE-1294).
- We should include a link to the RDOC for guidance on customer-triggered rollouts; propose we add the signed-bridge-agreement as a condition for waiving the notice requirement.

Approve the 40% credit. I’ll loop in Legal and CS to prepare the addendum; Sean, can you own scheduling the Ops review?

Laura
VP, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Claire Thomas <claire@edgewave.com>, ops@edgewave.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Final: Oct 29 partial degradation — credit and next steps

Claire — thanks for your patience while we analyzed this. Summary and final resolution:

- After correlating traces and customer logs, Redwood attributes 70% of the minute-weighted impact to issues in our edge proxy/cache eviction path and 30% to the rollout activities initiated by EdgeWave.
- Using the apportionment method described previously, Redwood will apply 21 chargeable downtime minutes for SLA credit calculation. Per the SLA credit table this results in a 40% service credit for November billing.

What we will do next:
1) Apply the 40% service credit to your Nov invoice and send a confirmation email with the credit breakdown.
2) Schedule an Ops review with your infra team (Sean Gallagher will reach out to find a time).
3) Provide a short addendum (signed-bridge-agreement.pdf) to waive the advance-notice requirement for this single event; Legal will send the doc for signature.

Attachments: edgewave-credit-calculation.csv (calculation breakdown), signed-bridge-agreement.pdf (addendum draft).

If you’d like a joint call this week to walk through traces, we can do that — Sean from our Ops team will coordinate.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0163

Note: This decision is a one-time apportionment and does not set a precedent for future maintenance windows.
